target.title: ci(cloudflare): deploy crawl-remote from protected ClawSweeper environment
target.body:
## Summary

- build and validate the exact current `openclaw/crawl-remote` `main` SHA on an unprivileged runner
- publish a bounded immutable release artifact, then consume it from a fresh protected runner that never executes target lifecycle code
- require the protected environment to explicitly assign deployment authority to ClawSweeper and bind a unique Cloudflare token by SHA-256 fingerprint
- bind observation-order and snapshot-provenance rollout states into artifact, manifest, receipt, D1 verification, and endpoint proof
- authenticate and prove the Access-gated custom route before any migration or deployment, then prove workers.dev after deployment
- capture the prior stable Worker version and roll traffic back on deploy failure, post-deploy `main` drift, or failed production proof
- package only the exact reviewed D1 migration sequence and SHA-256 content set
- fail closed unless crawl-remote's in-repository deploy workflow is absent, retired, or disabled

## Security boundary

- preflight receives no Cloudflare credential and mints only a repository-scoped read token
- production remains disabled unless `CRAWL_REMOTE_DEPLOY_AUTHORITY=clawsweeper-v1`
- credentialed steps accept only `CRAWL_REMOTE_PRODUCTION_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` from the protected environment and verify it against `CRAWL_REMOTE_CLOUDFLARE_TOKEN_SHA256`
- no repository-secret or generic-token fallback exists
- protected environment variables are resolved only inside protected steps; custom-route proof mode is mandatory and may be `disabled` or `access-service-token`
- exact current-main authorization runs before D1 mutation, before Worker deployment, and after Worker deployment
- missing pre-migration snapshot provenance is accepted only for a selected dormant bootstrap; post-migration proof requires both exact fence rows
- failed releases restore the exact previous 100% Worker version; forward D1 migrations remain applied and must preserve compatibility with both versions

## Coordinated authority cutover

Companion retirement PR: https://github.com/openclaw/crawl-remote/pull/37

1. Merge the companion PR to remove crawl-remote's service-owned production mutator.
2. Merge this PR while `CRAWL_REMOTE_DEPLOY_AUTHORITY` remains unset. The centralized path stays fail-closed.
3. Configure the protected `crawl-remote-production` environment with the authority value, unique token, token fingerprint, Access service-token credentials, and selected custom-route proof mode.
4. Dispatch only the then-current exact crawl-remote `main` SHA with both rollout states set to `dormant` for the first rollout.

## Validation

- exact reviewed head: `6c0704123fa7fdb2dd9ac8a467fa021c223514be`
- focused deployment workflow tests: 22/22
- pinned Wrangler `4.107.1` command and JSON-contract inspection
- real Wrangler dry-run rehearsal against the crawl-remote checkout; accepted `index.js`, `index.js.map`, and `README.md`, then packaged only `index.js`
- all seven current crawl-remote migrations pass the exact-name and exact-SHA-256 release packager
- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false run check` completed build and lint, then passed 952/953 unit tests; the unrelated close-time-note test failed only in the parallel suite and passed in isolation
- `git diff --check`

## Rollout status

No production rollout was attempted. The unique protected-environment Cloudflare token and its fingerprint still need operator provisioning; do not create a repository-level fallback.
